BitField.description: ADC voltage regulator ready flag of the slave ADC This bit is a copy of the LDORDY bit of the corresponding ADCx+1_ISR register.

BitField.name: DUAL
BitField.description: Dual ADC mode selection These bits are written by software to select the operating mode. All the ADCs are independent: The configurations 00001 to 01001 correspond to the following operating modes: Dual mode, master and slave ADCs working together: All other combinations are reserved and must not be programmed Note: The software is allowed to write these bits only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Combined regular simultaneous + injected simultaneous mode

Enum.name: B_0x2
Enum.description: Combined regular simultaneous + alternate trigger mode

Enum.name: B_0x3
Enum.description: Combined Interleaved mode + injected simultaneous mode

BitField.name: DELAY
BitField.description: Delay between the end of the master ADC sampling phase and the beginning of the slave ADC sampling phase. These bits are set and cleared by software. These bits are used in dual interleaved modes. Refer to for the value of ADC resolution versus DELAY bits values. Note: The software is allowed to write these bits only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).

BitField.name: DAMDF
BitField.description: Dual ADC Mode Data Format This bit-field is set and cleared by software. It specifies the data format in the common data register ADC12_CDR. Note: The software is allowed to write these bits only when ADSTART = 0 (which ensures that no regular conversion is ongoing).

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Dual ADC mode without data packing (ADC12_CDR and ADC12_CDR2 registers not used).

Enum.name: B_0x2
Enum.description: Data formatting mode for 32 down to 10-bit resolution

BitField.name: PRESC
BitField.description: ADC prescaler These bits are set and cleared by software to select the frequency of the ADC clock. The clock is common to all ADCs. Others: Reserved, must not be used Note: The software is allowed to write this bit only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).

BitField.name: VREFEN
BitField.description: VREFINT enable This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable the VREFINT buffer. Note: The software is allowed to write this bit only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).

BitField.name: VSENSESEL
BitField.description: Temperature sensor voltage selection This bit is set and cleared by software to control the temperature sensor channel. Note: The software is allowed to write this bit only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).

BitField.name: VBATEN
BitField.description: VBAT enable This bit is set and cleared by software to control the VBAT channel. Note: The software is allowed to write this bit only when the ADCs are disabled (ADCAL = 0, JADSTART = 0, ADSTART = 0, ADSTP = 0, ADDIS = 0 and ADEN = 0).

Register.name: ADC12_CDR
Register.description: ADC common regular data register for dual mode

BitField.name: RDATA_MST
BitField.description: Regular data of the master ADC. In dual mode, these bits contain the regular data of the master ADC. Refer to . The data alignment is applied as described in offset (ADC_DR, ADC_JDRy, OFFSETy, OFFSETy_CH, OVSS, LSHIFT, USAT, SSAT)) In DAMDF[1:0] = 11 mode, bits 15:8 contains SLV_ADC_DR[7:0], bits 7:0 contains MST_ADC_DR[7:0].

BitField.name: RDATA_SLV
BitField.description: Regular data of the slave ADC In dual mode, these bits contain the regular data of the slave ADC. Refer to Dual ADC modes. The data alignment is applied as described in offset (ADC_DR, ADC_JDRy, OFFSETy, OFFSETy_CH, OVSS, LSHIFT, USAT, SSAT))

Register.name: ADC12_CDR2
Register.description: ADC common regular data register for 32-bit dual mode

BitField.name: RDATA_ALT
BitField.description: Regular data of the master/slave alternated ADCs In dual mode, these bits alternatively contains the regular 32-bit data of the master and the slave ADC. Refer to . The data alignment is applied as described in (ADC_DR, ADC_JDRy, OFFSETy, OFFSETy_CH, OVSS, LSHIFT, USAT, SSAT).

BitField.name: VERSION
BitField.description: Version of the DSI Host This read-only register contains the version of the DSI Host

BitField.name: EN
BitField.description: Enable This bit configures the DSI Host in either power-up mode or to reset.

BitField.name: TXECKDIV
BitField.description: TX escape clock division This field indicates the division factor for the TX escape clock source (lanebyteclk). The values 0 and 1 stop the TX_ESC clock generation.

BitField.name: TOCKDIV
BitField.description: Timeout clock division This field indicates the division factor for the timeout clock used as the timing unit in the configuration of HS to LP and LP to HS transition error.

BitField.name: VCID
BitField.description: Virtual channel ID These bits configure the virtual channel ID for the LTDC interface traffic.

Register.name: DSI_LCOLCR
Register.description: DSI Host LTDC color coding register

BitField.name: COLC
BitField.description: Color coding This field configures the DPI color coding. Others: Reserved

BitField.name: LPE
BitField.description: Loosely packet enable This bit enables the loosely packed variant to 18-bit configuration

Register.name: DSI_LPCR
Register.description: DSI Host LTDC polarity configuration register

BitField.name: DEP
BitField.description: Data enable polarity This bit configures the polarity of data enable pin.

BitField.name: VSP
BitField.description: VSYNC polarity This bit configures the polarity of VSYNC pin.

BitField.name: HSP
BitField.description: HSYNC polarity This bit configures the polarity of HSYNC pin.

Register.name: DSI_LPMCR
Register.description: DSI Host low-power mode configuration register

BitField.name: VLPSIZE
BitField.description: VACT largest packet size This field is used for the transmission of commands in low-power mode. It defines the size, in bytes, of the largest packet that can fit in a line during VACT regions.

BitField.name: LPSIZE
BitField.description: Largest packet size This field is used for the transmission of commands in low-power mode. It defines the size, in bytes, of the largest packet that can fit in a line during VSA, VBP and VFP regions.

BitField.name: ETTXE
BitField.description: EoTp transmission enable This bit enables the EoTP transmission.

BitField.name: ETRXE
BitField.description: EoTp reception enable This bit enables the EoTp reception.

BitField.name: BTAE
BitField.description: Bus-turn-around enable This bit enables the bus-turn-around (BTA) request.

BitField.name: ECCRXE
BitField.description: ECC reception enable This bit enables the ECC reception, error correction and reporting.

BitField.name: CRCRXE
BitField.description: CRC reception enable This bit enables the CRC reception and error reporting.

BitField.name: ETTXLPE
BitField.description: EoTp transmission in low-power enable This bit enables the EoTP transmission in low-power.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: EoTp transmission in low-power is disabled.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: EoTp transmission in low-power is enabled.

BitField.name: VCIDRX
BitField.description: Virtual channel ID for reception This field indicates the generic interface read-back virtual channel identification.

BitField.name: NUMC
BitField.description: Number of chunks This register configures the number of chunks to be transmitted during a line period (a chunk consists of a video packet and a null packet). If set to 0 or 1, the video line is transmitted in a single packet. If set to 1, the packet is part of a chunk, so a null packet follows it if NPSIZE > 0. Otherwise, multiple chunks are used to transmit each video line.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR0
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 0

BitField.name: LPRX_TOCNT
BitField.description: Low-power reception timeout counter This field configures the timeout counter that triggers a low-power reception timeout contention detection (measured in TOCKDIV cycles).

BitField.name: HSTX_TOCNT
BitField.description: High-speed transmission timeout counter This field configures the timeout counter that triggers a high-speed transmission timeout contention detection (measured in TOCKDIV cycles). If using the non-burst mode and there is no enough time to switch from high-speed to low-power and back in the period from one line data finishing to the next line sync start, the DSI link returns the low-power state once per frame, then configure the TOCKDIV and HSTX_TOCNT to be in accordance with: HSTX_TOCNT * lanebyteclkperiod * TOCKDIV â¥ the time of one FRAME data transmission *Â (1 + 10%) In burst mode, RGB pixel packets are time-compressed, leaving more time during a scan line. Therefore, if in burst mode and there is enough time to switch from high-speed to low-power and back in the period from one line data finishing to the next line sync start, the DSI link can return low-power mode and back in this time interval to save power. For this, configure the TOCKDIV and HSTX_TOCNT to be in accordance with: HSTX_TOCNT * lanebyteclkperiod * TOCKDIV â¥ the time of one LINE data transmission *Â (1Â +Â 10%)

Register.name: DSI_TCCR1
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 1

BitField.name: HSRD_TOCNT
BitField.description: High-speed read timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link still, after sending a high-speed read operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR2
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 2

BitField.name: LPRD_TOCNT
BitField.description: Low-power read timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link still, after sending a low-power read operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR3
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 3

BitField.name: HSWR_TOCNT
BitField.description: High-speed write timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link inactive after sending a high-speed write operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

BitField.name: PM
BitField.description: Presp mode When set to 1, this bit ensures that the peripheral response timeout caused by HSWR_TOCNT is used only once per LTDC frame in command mode, when both the following conditions are met: dpivsync_edpiwms has risen and fallen. Packets originated from LTDC in command mode have been transmitted and its FIFO is empty again. In this scenario no non-LTDC command requests are sent to the D-PHY, even if there is traffic from generic interface ready to be sent, making it return to stop state. When it does so, PRESP_TO counter is activated and only when it finishes does the controller send any other traffic that is ready.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR4
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 4

BitField.name: LPWR_TOCNT
BitField.description: Low-power write timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link still, after sending a low-power write operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR5

BitField.name: DSIM
BitField.description: DSI mode This bit selects the mode for the video transmission. This bit must only be changed when DSI Host is stopped (DSI_CR.EN = 0).

BitField.name: COLMUX
BitField.description: Color multiplexing This bit selects the color multiplexing used by DSI Host. This field must only be changed when DSI is stopped (DSI_WCR.DSIEN = 0 and DSI_CR.ENÂ =Â 0).

BitField.name: TESRC
BitField.description: TE source This bit selects the tearing effect (TE) source. This bit must only be changed when DSI Host is stopped (DSI_CR.EN = 0).

BitField.name: TEPOL
BitField.description: TE polarity This bit selects the polarity of the external pin tearing effect (TE) source. This bit must only be changed when DSI Host is stopped (DSI_CR.EN = 0).

BitField.name: AR
BitField.description: Automatic refresh This bit selects the refresh mode in DBI mode. This bit must only be changed when DSI Host is stopped (DSI_CR.EN = 0).

BitField.name: VSPOL
BitField.description: VSync polarity This bit selects the VSync edge on which the LTDC is halted. This bit must only be changed when DSI is stopped (DSI_WCR.DSIEN = 0 and DSI_CR.ENÂ =Â 0).

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: LTDC halted on a falling edge

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: LTDC halted on a rising edge

BitField.name: CPLLUIF
BitField.description: Clear PLL unlock interrupt flag Write 1 clears the PLLUIF flag in the DSI_WSR register.

BitField.name: SWCL
BitField.description: Swap clock lane pins This bit swaps the pins on clock lane.

BitField.name: SWDL0
BitField.description: Swap data lane 0 pins This bit swaps the pins on data lane 0.

BitField.name: SWDL1
BitField.description: Swap data lane 1 pins This bit swaps the pins on clock lane.

BitField.name: FTXSMCL
BitField.description: Force in TX Stop mode the clock lane This bit forces the clock lane in TX stop mode. It is used to initialize a lane module in transmit mode. It causes the lane module to immediately jump to transmit control mode and to begin transmitting a stop state (LP-11). It can be used to go back in TX mode after a wrong BTA sequence.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Force the clock lane in TX Stop mode

BitField.name: FTXSMDL
BitField.description: Force in TX Stop mode the data lanes This bit forces the data lanes in TX stop mode. It is used to initialize a lane module in transmit mode. It causes the lane module to immediately jump to transmit control mode and to begin transmitting a stop state (LP-11). It can be used to go back in TX mode after a wrong BTA sequence.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Force the data lanes in TX Stop mode

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Return to low-power inside the VACT is disabled.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Return to low-power inside the VACT is enabled.

BitField.name: LPHBPE
BitField.description: Low-power horizontal back-porch enable This bit enables the return to low-power inside the horizontal back-porch (HBP) period when timing allows.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Return to low-power inside the HBP period is disabled.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Return to low-power inside the HBP period is enabled.

BitField.name: LPHFPE
BitField.description: Low-power horizontal front-porch enable This bit enables the return to low-power inside the horizontal front-porch (HFP) period when timing allows.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Return to low-power inside the HFP period is disabled.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Return to low-power inside the HFP period is enabled.

BitField.name: FBTAAE
BitField.description: Frame bus-turn-around acknowledge enable This bit enables the request for an acknowledge response at the end of a frame.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Acknowledge response at the end of a frame is disabled.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Acknowledge response at the end of a frame is enabled.

BitField.name: LPCE
BitField.description: Low-power command enable This bit enables the command transmission only in low-power mode.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Command transmission in low-power mode is disabled.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Command transmission in low-power mode is enabled.

Register.name: DSI_VPCR
Register.description: DSI Host video packet configuration register

BitField.name: VPSIZE
BitField.description: Video packet size This field configures the number of pixels in a single video packet. For 18-bit not loosely packed data types, this number must be a multiple of 4. For YCbCr data types, it must be a multiple of 2 as described in the DSI specification.

Register.name: DSI_VCCR
Register.description: DSI Host video chunks configuration register

BitField.name: NUMC
BitField.description: Number of chunks This register configures the number of chunks to be transmitted during a line period (a chunk consists of a video packet and a null packet). If set to 0 or 1, the video line is transmitted in a single packet. If set to 1, the packet is part of a chunk, so a null packet follows it if NPSIZE > 0. Otherwise, multiple chunks are used to transmit each video line.

Register.name: DSI_VNPCR
Register.description: DSI Host video null packet configuration register

BitField.name: NPSIZE
BitField.description: Null packet size This field configures the number of bytes inside a null packet. Setting to 0 disables the null packets.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR0
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 0

BitField.name: LPRX_TOCNT
BitField.description: Low-power reception timeout counter This field configures the timeout counter that triggers a low-power reception timeout contention detection (measured in TOCKDIV cycles).

BitField.name: HSTX_TOCNT
BitField.description: High-speed transmission timeout counter This field configures the timeout counter that triggers a high-speed transmission timeout contention detection (measured in TOCKDIV cycles). If using the non-burst mode and there is no enough time to switch from high-speed to low-power and back in the period from one line data finishing to the next line sync start, the DSI link returns the low-power state once per frame, then configure the TOCKDIV and HSTX_TOCNT to be in accordance with: HSTX_TOCNT * lanebyteclkperiod * TOCKDIV â¥ the time of one FRAME data transmission *Â (1 + 10%) In burst mode, RGB pixel packets are time-compressed, leaving more time during a scan line. Therefore, if in burst mode and there is enough time to switch from high-speed to low-power and back in the period from one line data finishing to the next line sync start, the DSI link can return low-power mode and back in this time interval to save power. For this, configure the TOCKDIV and HSTX_TOCNT to be in accordance with: HSTX_TOCNT * lanebyteclkperiod * TOCKDIV â¥ the time of one LINE data transmission *Â (1Â +Â 10%)

Register.name: DSI_TCCR1
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 1

BitField.name: HSRD_TOCNT
BitField.description: High-speed read timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link still, after sending a high-speed read operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR2
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 2

BitField.name: LPRD_TOCNT
BitField.description: Low-power read timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link still, after sending a low-power read operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR3
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 3

BitField.name: HSWR_TOCNT
BitField.description: High-speed write timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link inactive after sending a high-speed write operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

BitField.name: PM
BitField.description: Presp mode When set to 1, this bit ensures that the peripheral response timeout caused by HSWR_TOCNT is used only once per LTDC frame in command mode, when both the following conditions are met: dpivsync_edpiwms has risen and fallen. Packets originated from LTDC in command mode have been transmitted and its FIFO is empty again. In this scenario no non-LTDC command requests are sent to the D-PHY, even if there is traffic from generic interface ready to be sent, making it return to stop state. When it does so, PRESP_TO counter is activated and only when it finishes does the controller send any other traffic that is ready.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR4
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 4

BitField.name: LPWR_TOCNT
BitField.description: Low-power write timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link still, after sending a low-power write operation. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the D-PHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

Register.name: DSI_TCCR5
Register.description: DSI Host timeout counter configuration register 5

BitField.name: BTA_TOCNT
BitField.description: Bus-turn-around timeout counter This field sets a period for which the DSI Host keeps the link still, after completing a bus-turn-around. This period is measured in cycles of lanebyteclk. The counting starts when the DâPHY enters the Stop state and causes no interrupts.

BitField.name: AR

BitField.name: VSPOL

BitField.name: CPLLUIF
BitField.description: Clear PLL unlock interrupt flag Write 1 clears the PLLUIF flag in the DSI_WSR register.

BitField.name: SWCL
BitField.description: Swap clock lane pins This bit swaps the pins on clock lane.

BitField.name: SWDL0
BitField.description: Swap data lane 0 pins This bit swaps the pins on data lane 0.

BitField.name: SWDL1
BitField.description: Swap data lane 1 pins This bit swaps the pins on clock lane.

BitField.name: FTXSMCL
BitField.description: Force in TX Stop mode the clock lane This bit forces the clock lane in TX stop mode. It is used to initialize a lane module in transmit mode. It causes the lane module to immediately jump to transmit control mode and to begin transmitting a stop state (LP-11). It can be used to go back in TX mode after a wrong BTA sequence.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Force the clock lane in TX Stop mode

BitField.name: FTXSMDL
BitField.description: Force in TX Stop mode the data lanes This bit forces the data lanes in TX stop mode. It is used to initialize a lane module in transmit mode. It causes the lane module to immediately jump to transmit control mode and to begin transmitting a stop state (LP-11). It can be used to go back in TX mode after a wrong BTA sequence.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Force the data lanes in TX Stop mode

BitField.name: RT0
BitField.description: Rising trigger event configuration bit of configurable event input x When EXTI_SECCFGR.SECx is disabled, RTx can be accessed with non-secure and secure access. When EXTI_SECCFGR.SECx is enabled, RTx can only be accessed with secure access. Non-secure write to this bit x is discarded and non-secure read returns 0. When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is disabled, RTx can be accessed with unprivileged and privileged access. When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is enabled, RTx can only be accessed with privileged access. Unprivileged write to this bit x is discarded, unprivileged read returns 0. Note: RT25, RT24, and RT23 bits are only available on some devices in the STM32U5 Series. Refer to the EXTI line connections table for its availability. If not present, consider this bit as reserved and keep at reset value.

When EXTI_SECCFGR.SECx is enabled, PRIVx can only be written with secure access. Non-secure write to this PRIVx is discarded. Note: PRIV25, PRIV24, and PRIV23 bits are only available on some devices in the STM32U5 Series. Refer to the EXTI line connections table for its availability. If not present, consider this bit as reserved and keep at reset value.

Enum.description: Security and privilege configuration locked, can no longer be modified.

Register.name: EXTI_IMR1
Register.description: EXTI CPU wake-up with interrupt mask register

BitField.name: IM0
BitField.description: CPU wake-up with interrupt mask on event input x When EXTI_SECCFGR.SECx is disabled, IMx can be accessed with non-secure and secure access. When EXTI_SECCFGR.SECx is enabled, IMx can only be accessed with secure access. Non-secure write to this bit is discarded and non-secure read returns 0. When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is disabled, IMx can be accessed with privileged and unprivileged access. When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is enabled, IMx can only be accessed with privileged access. Unprivileged write to this bit is discarded. Note: IM25, IM24, and IM23 bits are only available on some devices in the STM32U5 Series. Refer to the EXTI line connections table for its availability. If not present, consider this bit as reserved and keep at reset value.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Wake-up with interrupt request from input event x is masked.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Wake-up with interrupt request from input event x is unmasked.

When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is disabled, SWIx can be accessed with unprivileged and privileged access. When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is enabled, SWIx can only be accessed with privileged access. Unprivileged write to this SWIx is discarded, unprivileged read returns 0. A software interrupt is generated independent from the setting in EXTI_RTSR and EXTI_FTSR. It always returns 0 when read. Note: SW25, SW24, and SW23 bits are only available on some devices in the STM32U5 Series. Refer to the EXTI line connections table for its availability. If not present, consider this bit as reserved and keep at reset value.

When EXTI_SECCFGR.SECx is enabled, RPIFx can only be accessed with secure access. Non-secure write to this RPIFx is discarded, non-secure read returns 0. When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is disabled, RPIFx can be accessed with unprivileged and privileged access. When EXTI_PRIVCFGR.PRIVx is enabled, RPIFx can only be accessed with privileged access. Unprivileged write to this RPIFx is discarded, unprivileged read returns 0. This bit is set when the rising edge event or an EXTI_SWIER software trigger arrives on the configurable event line. This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it. RPIF25, RPIF24, and RPIF23 bits are only available on some devices in the STM32U5 Series. Refer to the EXTI line connections table for its availability. Note: If not present, consider this bit as reserved and keep at reset value.

BitField.name: LATENCY
BitField.description: Latency These bits represent the ratio between the HCLK (AHB clock) period and the Flash memory access time. ...

BitField.name: PRFTEN
BitField.description: Prefetch enable This bit enables the prefetch buffer in the embedded Flash memory.

BitField.name: LPM
BitField.description: Low-power read mode This bit puts the Flash memory in low-power read mode.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Flash not in low-power read mode

BitField.name: PDREQ1
BitField.description: Bank 1 power-down mode request This bit is write-protected with FLASH_PDKEY1R. This bit requests bank 1 to enter power-down mode. When bank 1 enters power-down mode, this bit is cleared by hardware and the PDKEY1R is locked.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: No request for bank 1 to enter power-down mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 1 requested to enter power-down mode

BitField.name: PDREQ2
BitField.description: Bank 2 power-down mode request This bit is write-protected with FLASH_PDKEY2R. This bit requests bank 2 to enter power-down mode. When bank 2 enters power-down mode, this bit is cleared by hardware and the PDKEY2R is locked.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: No request for bank 2 to enter power-down mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 2 requested to enter power-down mode

BitField.name: SLEEP_PD
BitField.description: Flash memory power-down mode during Sleep mode This bit determines whether the Flash memory is in power-down mode or Idle mode when the device is in Sleep mode. The Flash must not be put in power-down while a program or an erase operation is on-going.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Flash in Idle mode during Sleep mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Flash in power-down mode during Sleep mode

BitField.name: NSKEY
BitField.description: Flash memory non-secure key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the FLASH_NSCR register, allowing the Flash memory non-secure programming/erasing operations: KEY1: 0x4567 0123 KEY2: 0xCDEF 89AB

BitField.name: SECKEY
BitField.description: Flash memory secure key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the FLASH_SECCR register, allowing the Flash memory secure programming/erasing operations: KEY1: 0x4567 0123 KEY2: 0xCDEF 89AB

BitField.name: OPTKEY
BitField.description: Option byte key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the FLASH_OPTR register allowing option byte programming/erasing operations: KEY1: 0x0819 2A3B KEY2: 0x4C5D 6E7F

BitField.name: PDKEY1
BitField.description: Bank 1 power-down key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the PDREQ1 bit in FLASH_ACR: PDKEY1_1: 0x0415 2637 PDKEY1_2: 0xFAFB FCFD

BitField.name: PDKEY2
BitField.description: Bank 2 power-down key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the PDREQ2 bit in FLASH_ACR: PDKEY2_1: 0x4051 6273 PDKEY2_2: 0xAFBF CFDF

BitField.name: EOP
BitField.description: Non-secure end of operation This bit is set by hardware when one or more Flash memory non-secure operation (program/erase) has been completed successfully. This bit is set only if the non-secure end of operation interrupts are enabled (EOPIE = 1 in FLASH_NSCR). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: OPERR
BitField.description: Non-secure operation error This bit is set by hardware when a Flash memory non-secure operation (program/erase) completes unsuccessfully. This bit is set only if non-secure error interrupts are enabled (NSERRIE = 1). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PROGERR
BitField.description: Non-secure programming error This bit is set by hardware when a non-secure quad-word address to be programmed contains a value different from all 1 before programming, except if the data to write is all 0. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: WRPERR
BitField.description: Non-secure write protection error This bit is set by hardware when an non-secure address to be erased/programmed belongs to a write-protected part (by WRP, PCROP, HDP or RDP level 1) of the Flash memory. This bit is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: PGAERR
BitField.description: Non-secure programming alignment error This bit is set by hardware when the first word to be programmed is not aligned with a quad-word address, or the second, third or forth word does not belong to the same quad-word address. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: SIZERR
BitField.description: Non-secure size error This bit is set by hardware when the size of the access is a byte or half-word during a non-secure program sequence. Only quad-word programming is allowed by means of successive word accesses. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PGSERR
BitField.description: Non-secure programming sequence error This bit is set by hardware when programming sequence is not correct. It is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: OPTWERR
BitField.description: Option write error This bit is set by hardware when the options bytes are written with an invalid configuration. It is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: BSY
BitField.description: Non-secure busy This indicates that a Flash memory secure or non-secure operation is in progress. This bit is set at the beginning of a Flash operation and reset when the operation finishes or when an error occurs.

BitField.name: WDW
BitField.description: Non-secure wait data to write This bit indicates that the Flash memory write buffer has been written by a secure or non-secure operation. It is set when the first data is stored in the buffer and cleared when the write is performed in the Flash memory.

BitField.name: OEM1LOCK
BitField.description: OEM1 lock This bit indicates that the OEM1 RDP key read during the OBL is not virgin. When set, the OEM1 RDP lock mechanism is active.

BitField.name: OEM2LOCK
BitField.description: OEM2 lock This bit indicates that the OEM2 RDP key read during the OBL is not virgin. When set, the OEM2 RDP lock mechanism is active.

BitField.name: PD1
BitField.description: Bank 1 in power-down mode This bit indicates that the Flash memory bank 1 is in power-down state. It is reset when bank 1 is in normal mode or being awaken.

BitField.name: PD2
BitField.description: Bank 2 in power-down mode This bit indicates that the Flash memory bank 2 is in power-down state. It is reset when bank 2 is in normal mode or being awaken.

BitField.name: EOP
BitField.description: Secure end of operation This bit is set by hardware when one or more Flash memory secure operation (program/erase) has been completed successfully. This bit is set only if the secure end of operation interrupts are enabled (EOPIE = 1 in FLASH_SECCR). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: OPERR
BitField.description: Secure operation error This bit is set by hardware when a Flash memory secure operation (program/erase) completes unsuccessfully. This bit is set only if secure error interrupts are enabled (SECERRIE = 1). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PROGERR
BitField.description: Secure programming error This bit is set by hardware when a secure quad-word address to be programmed contains a value different from all 1 before programming, except if the data to write is all 0. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: WRPERR
BitField.description: Secure write protection error This bit is set by hardware when an secure address to be erased/programmed belongs to a write-protected part (by WRP, PCROP, HDP or RDP level 1) of the Flash memory.This bit is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: PGAERR
BitField.description: Secure programming alignment error This bit is set by hardware when the first word to be programmed is not aligned with a quad-word address, or the second, third or forth word does not belong to the same quad-word address.This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: SIZERR
BitField.description: Secure size error This bit is set by hardware when the size of the access is a byte or half-word during a secure program sequence. Only quad-word programming is allowed by means of successive word accesses.This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PGSERR
BitField.description: Secure programming sequence error This bit is set by hardware when programming sequence is not correct. It is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: RDERR
BitField.description: Secure readout protection error This bit is set by hardware when a read access is performed to a secure PCROP area and when a cacheable fetch access is performed to a secure PCROP area. An interrupt is generated if RDERRIE is set in FLASH_SECCR register. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: BSY
BitField.description: Secure busy This bit indicates that a Flash memory secure or non-secure operation is in progress. This is set on the beginning of a Flash operation and reset when the operation finishes or when an error occurs.

BitField.name: WDW
BitField.description: Secure wait data to write This bit indicates that the Flash memory write buffer has been written by a secure or non-secure operation. It is set when the first data is stored in the buffer and cleared when the write is performed in the Flash memory.

BitField.name: PG
BitField.description: Non-secure programming

BitField.name: PER
BitField.description: Non-secure page erase

BitField.name: MER1
BitField.description: Non-secure bank 1 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 1 non-secure mass erase (all bank 1 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: PNB
BitField.description: Non-secure page number selection These bits select the page to erase. ... ...

BitField.name: BKER
BitField.description: Non-secure bank selection for page erase

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Bank 1 selected for non-secure page erase

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 2 selected for non-secure page erase

BitField.name: BWR
BitField.description: Non-secure burst write programming mode When set, this bit selects the burst write programming mode.

BitField.name: MER2
BitField.description: Non-secure bank 2 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 2 non-secure mass erase (all bank 2 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: STRT
BitField.description: Non-secure start This bit triggers a non-secure erase operation when set. If MER1, MER2 and PER bits are reset and the STRT bit is set, the PGSERR bit in FLASH_NSSR is set (this condition is forbidden). This bit is set only by software and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_NSSR.

BitField.name: OPTSTRT
BitField.description: Options modification start This bit triggers an options operation when set. It can not be written if OPTLOCK bit is set. This bit is set only by software, and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_NSSR.

BitField.name: EOPIE
BitField.description: Non-secure end of operation interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the EOP bit in the FLASH_NSSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: ERRIE
BitField.description: Non-secure error interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the OPERR bit in the FLASH_NSSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: OBL_LAUNCH
BitField.description: Force the option byte loading When set to 1, this bit forces the option byte reloading. This bit is cleared only when the option byte loading is complete. It cannot be written if OPTLOCK is set.

BitField.name: OPTLOCK
BitField.description: Option lock This bit is set only. When set, all bits concerning user options in FLASH_NSCR register are locked. This bit is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence. The LOCK bit in the FLASH_NSCR must be cleared before doing the unlock sequence for OPTLOCK bit. In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next reset.

BitField.name: LOCK
BitField.description: Non-secure lock This bit is set only. When set, the FLASH_NSCR register is locked. It is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence in FLASH_NSKEYR register. In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next system reset.

BitField.name: PG
BitField.description: Secure programming

BitField.name: PER
BitField.description: Secure page erase

BitField.name: MER1
BitField.description: Secure bank 1 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 1 secure mass erase (all bank 1 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: PNB
BitField.description: Secure page number selection These bits select the page to erase. ... ...

BitField.name: BKER
BitField.description: Secure bank selection for page erase

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Bank 1 selected for secure page erase

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 2 selected for secure page erase

BitField.name: BWR
BitField.description: Secure burst write programming mode When set, this bit selects the burst write programming mode.

BitField.name: MER2
BitField.description: Secure bank 2 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 2 secure mass erase (all bank 2 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: STRT
BitField.description: Secure start This bit triggers a secure erase operation when set. If MER1, MER2 and PER bits are reset and the STRT bit is set, the PGSERR in the FLASH_SECSR is set (this condition is forbidden). This bit is set only by software and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_SECSR.

BitField.name: EOPIE
BitField.description: Secure End of operation interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the EOP bit in the FLASH_SECSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: ERRIE
BitField.description: Secure error interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the OPERR bit in the FLASH_SECSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: RDERRIE
BitField.description: Secure PCROP read error interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the RDERR bit in the FLASH_SECSR is set to 1.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Secure PCROP read error interrupt disabled

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Secure PCROP read error interrupt enabled

BitField.name: INV
BitField.description: Flash memory security state invert This bit inverts the Flash memory security state.

BitField.name: LOCK
BitField.description: Secure lock This bit is set only. When set, the FLASH_SECCR register is locked. It is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence in FLASH_SECKEYR register. In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next system reset.

BitField.name: ADDR_ECC
BitField.description: ECC fail address This field indicates which address is concerned by the ECC error correction or by the double ECC error detection. The address is given by bank from address 0x0 0000 to 0x1F FFF0.

BitField.name: BK_ECC
BitField.description: ECC fail bank This bit indicates which bank is concerned by the ECC error correction or by the double ECC error detection.

BitField.name: SYSF_ECC
BitField.description: System Flash memory ECC fail This bit indicates that the ECC error correction or double ECC error detection is located in the system Flash memory.

BitField.name: ECCIE
BitField.description: ECC correction interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the ECCC bit in the FLASH_ECCR register is set.

BitField.name: ECCC
BitField.description: ECC correction This bit is set by hardware when one ECC error has been detected and corrected (only if ECCC and ECCD were previously cleared). An interrupt is generated if ECCIE is set. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: ECCD
BitField.description: ECC detection This bit is set by hardware when two ECC errors have been detected (only if ECCC and ECCD were previously cleared). When this bit is set, a NMI is generated. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: ADDR_OP
BitField.description: Interrupted operation address This field indicates which address in the Flash memory was accessed when reset occurred. The address is given by bank from address 0x0 0000 to 0x1F FFF0.

BitField.name: BK_OP
BitField.description: Interrupted operation bank This bit indicates which Flash memory bank was accessed when reset occurred

BitField.name: SYSF_OP
BitField.description: Operation in system Flash memory interrupted This bit indicates that the reset occurred during an operation in the system Flash memory.

BitField.name: CODE_OP
BitField.description: Flash memory operation code This field indicates which Flash memory operation has been interrupted by a system reset:

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: No Flash operation interrupted by previous reset

BitField.name: RDP
BitField.description: Readout protection level Others: Level 1 (memories readout protection active) Note: Refer to for more details.

Enum.name: B_0x55
Enum.description: Level 0.5 (readout protection not active, only non-secure debug access is possible). Only available when TrustZone is active (TZEN=1)

BitField.name: BOR_LEV
BitField.description: BOR reset level These bits contain the VDD supply level threshold that activates/releases the reset.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: BOR level 0 (reset level threshold around 1.7 V)

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: BOR level 1 (reset level threshold around 2.0 V)

Enum.name: B_0x2
Enum.description: BOR level 2 (reset level threshold around 2.2 V)

Enum.name: B_0x3
Enum.description: BOR level 3 (reset level threshold around 2.5 V)

Enum.name: B_0x4
Enum.description: BOR level 4 (reset level threshold around 2.8 V)

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: No reset generate when entering the Standby mode

BitField.description: Reset generation in Shutdown mode

BitField.name: NSBOOTADD0
BitField.description: Non-secure boot base address 0 The non-secure boot memory address can be programmed to any address in the valid address range with a granularity of 128 bytes. These bits correspond to address [31:7]. The NSBOOTADD0 option bytes are selected following the BOOT0 pin or nSWBOOT0 state. Examples: NSBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x0100000: Boot from non-secure Flash memory (0x0800 0000) NSBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x017F200: Boot from system memory bootloader (0x0BF9 0000) NSBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x0400000: Boot from non-secure SRAM1 on S-Bus (0x2000 0000)

BitField.name: NSBOOTADD1
BitField.description: Non-secure boot address 1 The non-secure boot memory address can be programmed to any address in the valid address range with a granularity of 128 bytes. These bits correspond to address [31:7]. The NSBOOTADD0 option bytes are selected following the BOOT0 pin or nSWBOOT0 state. Examples: NSBOOTADD1[24:0] = 0x0100000: Boot from non-secure Flash memory (0x0800 0000) NSBOOTADD1[24:0] = 0x017F200: Boot from system memory bootloader (0x0BF9 0000) NSBOOTADD1[24:0] = 0x0400000: Boot from non-secure SRAM1 on S-Bus (0x2000 0000)

BitField.name: BOOT_LOCK
BitField.description: Boot lock When set, the boot is always forced to base address value programmed in SECBOOTADD0[24:0] option bytes whatever the boot selection option. When set, this bit can only be cleared by an RDP at level 0.

BitField.name: SECBOOTADD0
BitField.description: Secure boot base address 0 The secure boot memory address can be programmed to any address in the valid address range with a granularity of 128 bytes. This bits correspond to address [31:7] The SECBOOTADD0 option bytes are selected following the BOOT0 pin or nSWBOOT0 state. Examples: SECBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x018 0000: Boot from secure Flash memory (0x0C00 0000) SECBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x01F F000: Boot from RSS (0x0FF8 0000) SECBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x060 0000: Boot from secure SRAM1 on S-Bus (0x3000 0000)

BitField.name: LATENCY
BitField.description: Latency These bits represent the ratio between the HCLK (AHB clock) period and the Flash memory access time. ...

BitField.name: PRFTEN
BitField.description: Prefetch enable This bit enables the prefetch buffer in the embedded Flash memory.

BitField.name: LPM
BitField.description: Low-power read mode This bit puts the Flash memory in low-power read mode.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Flash not in low-power read mode

BitField.name: PDREQ1
BitField.description: Bank 1 power-down mode request This bit is write-protected with FLASH_PDKEY1R. This bit requests bank 1 to enter power-down mode. When bank 1 enters power-down mode, this bit is cleared by hardware and the PDKEY1R is locked.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: No request for bank 1 to enter power-down mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 1 requested to enter power-down mode

BitField.name: PDREQ2
BitField.description: Bank 2 power-down mode request This bit is write-protected with FLASH_PDKEY2R. This bit requests bank 2 to enter power-down mode. When bank 2 enters power-down mode, this bit is cleared by hardware and the PDKEY2R is locked.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: No request for bank 2 to enter power-down mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 2 requested to enter power-down mode

BitField.name: SLEEP_PD
BitField.description: Flash memory power-down mode during Sleep mode This bit determines whether the Flash memory is in power-down mode or Idle mode when the device is in Sleep mode. The Flash must not be put in power-down while a program or an erase operation is on-going.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Flash in Idle mode during Sleep mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Flash in power-down mode during Sleep mode

BitField.name: NSKEY
BitField.description: Flash memory non-secure key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the FLASH_NSCR register, allowing the Flash memory non-secure programming/erasing operations: KEY1: 0x4567 0123 KEY2: 0xCDEF 89AB

BitField.name: SECKEY
BitField.description: Flash memory secure key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the FLASH_SECCR register, allowing the Flash memory secure programming/erasing operations: KEY1: 0x4567 0123 KEY2: 0xCDEF 89AB

BitField.name: OPTKEY
BitField.description: Option byte key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the FLASH_OPTR register allowing option byte programming/erasing operations: KEY1: 0x0819 2A3B KEY2: 0x4C5D 6E7F

BitField.name: PDKEY1
BitField.description: Bank 1 power-down key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the PDREQ1 bit in FLASH_ACR: PDKEY1_1: 0x0415 2637 PDKEY1_2: 0xFAFB FCFD

BitField.name: PDKEY2
BitField.description: Bank 2 power-down key The following values must be written consecutively to unlock the PDREQ2 bit in FLASH_ACR: PDKEY2_1: 0x4051 6273 PDKEY2_2: 0xAFBF CFDF

BitField.name: EOP
BitField.description: Non-secure end of operation This bit is set by hardware when one or more Flash memory non-secure operation (program/erase) has been completed successfully. This bit is set only if the non-secure end of operation interrupts are enabled (EOPIE = 1 in FLASH_NSCR). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: OPERR
BitField.description: Non-secure operation error This bit is set by hardware when a Flash memory non-secure operation (program/erase) completes unsuccessfully. This bit is set only if non-secure error interrupts are enabled (NSERRIE = 1). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PROGERR
BitField.description: Non-secure programming error This bit is set by hardware when a non-secure quad-word address to be programmed contains a value different from all 1 before programming, except if the data to write is all 0. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: WRPERR
BitField.description: Non-secure write protection error This bit is set by hardware when an non-secure address to be erased/programmed belongs to a write-protected part (by WRP, PCROP, HDP or RDP level 1) of the Flash memory. This bit is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: PGAERR
BitField.description: Non-secure programming alignment error This bit is set by hardware when the first word to be programmed is not aligned with a quad-word address, or the second, third or forth word does not belong to the same quad-word address. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: SIZERR
BitField.description: Non-secure size error This bit is set by hardware when the size of the access is a byte or half-word during a non-secure program sequence. Only quad-word programming is allowed by means of successive word accesses. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PGSERR
BitField.description: Non-secure programming sequence error This bit is set by hardware when programming sequence is not correct. It is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: OPTWERR
BitField.description: Option write error This bit is set by hardware when the options bytes are written with an invalid configuration. It is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: BSY
BitField.description: Non-secure busy This indicates that a Flash memory secure or non-secure operation is in progress. This bit is set at the beginning of a Flash operation and reset when the operation finishes or when an error occurs.

BitField.name: WDW
BitField.description: Non-secure wait data to write This bit indicates that the Flash memory write buffer has been written by a secure or non-secure operation. It is set when the first data is stored in the buffer and cleared when the write is performed in the Flash memory.

BitField.name: OEM1LOCK
BitField.description: OEM1 lock This bit indicates that the OEM1 RDP key read during the OBL is not virgin. When set, the OEM1 RDP lock mechanism is active.

BitField.name: OEM2LOCK
BitField.description: OEM2 lock This bit indicates that the OEM2 RDP key read during the OBL is not virgin. When set, the OEM2 RDP lock mechanism is active.

BitField.name: PD1
BitField.description: Bank 1 in power-down mode This bit indicates that the Flash memory bank 1 is in power-down state. It is reset when bank 1 is in normal mode or being awaken.

BitField.name: PD2
BitField.description: Bank 2 in power-down mode This bit indicates that the Flash memory bank 2 is in power-down state. It is reset when bank 2 is in normal mode or being awaken.

BitField.name: EOP
BitField.description: Secure end of operation This bit is set by hardware when one or more Flash memory secure operation (program/erase) has been completed successfully. This bit is set only if the secure end of operation interrupts are enabled (EOPIE = 1 in FLASH_SECCR). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: OPERR
BitField.description: Secure operation error This bit is set by hardware when a Flash memory secure operation (program/erase) completes unsuccessfully. This bit is set only if secure error interrupts are enabled (SECERRIE = 1). This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PROGERR
BitField.description: Secure programming error This bit is set by hardware when a secure quad-word address to be programmed contains a value different from all 1 before programming, except if the data to write is all 0. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: WRPERR
BitField.description: Secure write protection error This bit is set by hardware when an secure address to be erased/programmed belongs to a write-protected part (by WRP, PCROP, HDP or RDP level 1) of the Flash memory.This bit is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: PGAERR
BitField.description: Secure programming alignment error This bit is set by hardware when the first word to be programmed is not aligned with a quad-word address, or the second, third or forth word does not belong to the same quad-word address.This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: SIZERR
BitField.description: Secure size error This bit is set by hardware when the size of the access is a byte or half-word during a secure program sequence. Only quad-word programming is allowed by means of successive word accesses.This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: PGSERR
BitField.description: Secure programming sequence error This bit is set by hardware when programming sequence is not correct. It is cleared by writing 1. Refer to for full conditions of error flag setting.

BitField.name: RDERR
BitField.description: Secure readout protection error This bit is set by hardware when a read access is performed to a secure PCROP area and when a cacheable fetch access is performed to a secure PCROP area. An interrupt is generated if RDERRIE is set in FLASH_SECCR register. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: BSY
BitField.description: Secure busy This bit indicates that a Flash memory secure or non-secure operation is in progress. This is set on the beginning of a Flash operation and reset when the operation finishes or when an error occurs.

BitField.name: WDW
BitField.description: Secure wait data to write This bit indicates that the Flash memory write buffer has been written by a secure or non-secure operation. It is set when the first data is stored in the buffer and cleared when the write is performed in the Flash memory.

BitField.description: Non-secure programming

BitField.name: PER
BitField.description: Non-secure page erase

BitField.name: MER1
BitField.description: Non-secure bank 1 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 1 non-secure mass erase (all bank 1 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: PNB
BitField.description: Non-secure page number selection These bits select the page to erase. ... ...

BitField.name: BKER
BitField.description: Non-secure bank selection for page erase

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Bank 1 selected for non-secure page erase

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 2 selected for non-secure page erase

BitField.name: BWR
BitField.description: Non-secure burst write programming mode When set, this bit selects the burst write programming mode.

BitField.name: MER2
BitField.description: Non-secure bank 2 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 2 non-secure mass erase (all bank 2 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: STRT
BitField.description: Non-secure start This bit triggers a non-secure erase operation when set. If MER1, MER2 and PER bits are reset and the STRT bit is set, the PGSERR bit in FLASH_NSSR is set (this condition is forbidden). This bit is set only by software and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_NSSR.

BitField.name: OPTSTRT
BitField.description: Options modification start This bit triggers an options operation when set. It can not be written if OPTLOCK bit is set. This bit is set only by software, and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_NSSR.

BitField.name: EOPIE
BitField.description: Non-secure end of operation interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the EOP bit in the FLASH_NSSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: ERRIE
BitField.description: Non-secure error interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the OPERR bit in the FLASH_NSSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: OBL_LAUNCH
BitField.description: Force the option byte loading When set to 1, this bit forces the option byte reloading. This bit is cleared only when the option byte loading is complete. It cannot be written if OPTLOCK is set.

BitField.name: OPTLOCK
BitField.description: Option lock This bit is set only. When set, all bits concerning user options in FLASH_NSCR register are locked. This bit is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence. The LOCK bit in the FLASH_NSCR must be cleared before doing the unlock sequence for OPTLOCK bit. In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next reset.

BitField.name: LOCK
BitField.description: Non-secure lock This bit is set only. When set, the FLASH_NSCR register is locked. It is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence in FLASH_NSKEYR register. In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next system reset.

BitField.name: PG
BitField.description: Secure programming

BitField.name: PER
BitField.description: Secure page erase

BitField.name: MER1
BitField.description: Secure bank 1 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 1 secure mass erase (all bank 1 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: PNB
BitField.description: Secure page number selection These bits select the page to erase. ... ...

BitField.name: BKER
BitField.description: Secure bank selection for page erase

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Bank 1 selected for secure page erase

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Bank 2 selected for secure page erase

BitField.name: BWR
BitField.description: Secure burst write programming mode When set, this bit selects the burst write programming mode.

BitField.name: MER2
BitField.description: Secure bank 2 mass erase This bit triggers the bank 2 secure mass erase (all bank 2 user pages) when set.

BitField.name: STRT
BitField.description: Secure start This bit triggers a secure erase operation when set. If MER1, MER2 and PER bits are reset and the STRT bit is set, the PGSERR in the FLASH_SECSR is set (this condition is forbidden). This bit is set only by software and is cleared when the BSY bit is cleared in FLASH_SECSR.

BitField.name: EOPIE
BitField.description: Secure End of operation interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the EOP bit in the FLASH_SECSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: ERRIE
BitField.description: Secure error interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the OPERR bit in the FLASH_SECSR is set to 1.

BitField.name: RDERRIE
BitField.description: Secure PCROP read error interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the RDERR bit in the FLASH_SECSR is set to 1.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Secure PCROP read error interrupt disabled

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: Secure PCROP read error interrupt enabled

BitField.name: INV
BitField.description: Flash memory security state invert This bit inverts the Flash memory security state.

BitField.name: LOCK
BitField.description: Secure lock This bit is set only. When set, the FLASH_SECCR register is locked. It is cleared by hardware after detecting the unlock sequence in FLASH_SECKEYR register. In case of an unsuccessful unlock operation, this bit remains set until the next system reset.

BitField.name: ADDR_ECC
BitField.description: ECC fail address This field indicates which address is concerned by the ECC error correction or by the double ECC error detection. The address is given by bank from address 0x0 0000 to 0x1F FFF0.

BitField.name: BK_ECC
BitField.description: ECC fail bank This bit indicates which bank is concerned by the ECC error correction or by the double ECC error detection.

BitField.name: SYSF_ECC
BitField.description: System Flash memory ECC fail This bit indicates that the ECC error correction or double ECC error detection is located in the system Flash memory.

BitField.name: ECCIE
BitField.description: ECC correction interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt generation when the ECCC bit in the FLASH_ECCR register is set.

BitField.name: ECCC
BitField.description: ECC correction This bit is set by hardware when one ECC error has been detected and corrected (only if ECCC and ECCD were previously cleared). An interrupt is generated if ECCIE is set. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: ECCD
BitField.description: ECC detection This bit is set by hardware when two ECC errors have been detected (only if ECCC and ECCD were previously cleared). When this bit is set, a NMI is generated. This bit is cleared by writing 1.

BitField.name: ADDR_OP
BitField.description: Interrupted operation address This field indicates which address in the Flash memory was accessed when reset occurred. The address is given by bank from address 0x0 0000 to 0x1F FFF0.

BitField.name: BK_OP
BitField.description: Interrupted operation bank This bit indicates which Flash memory bank was accessed when reset occurred

BitField.name: SYSF_OP
BitField.description: Operation in system Flash memory interrupted This bit indicates that the reset occurred during an operation in the system Flash memory.

BitField.name: CODE_OP
BitField.description: Flash memory operation code This field indicates which Flash memory operation has been interrupted by a system reset:

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: No Flash operation interrupted by previous reset

BitField.name: RDP
BitField.description: Readout protection level Others: Level 1 (memories readout protection active) Note: Refer to for more details.

Enum.name: B_0x55
Enum.description: Level 0.5 (readout protection not active, only non-secure debug access is possible). Only available when TrustZone is active (TZEN=1)

BitField.name: BOR_LEV
BitField.description: BOR reset level These bits contain the VDD supply level threshold that activates/releases the reset.

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: BOR level 0 (reset level threshold around 1.7 V)

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: BOR level 1 (reset level threshold around 2.0 V)

Enum.name: B_0x2
Enum.description: BOR level 2 (reset level threshold around 2.2 V)

Enum.name: B_0x3
Enum.description: BOR level 3 (reset level threshold around 2.5 V)

Enum.name: B_0x4
Enum.description: BOR level 4 (reset level threshold around 2.8 V)

BitField.name: nRST_STOP
BitField.description: Reset generation in Stop mode

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Reset generated when entering the Stop mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: No reset generated when entering the Stop mode

BitField.name: nRST_STDBY
BitField.description: Reset generation in Standby mode

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Reset generated when entering the Standby mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: No reset generate when entering the Standby mode

BitField.name: nRST_SHDW
BitField.description: Reset generation in Shutdown mode

Enum.name: B_0x0
Enum.description: Reset generated when entering the Shutdown mode

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: No reset generated when entering the Shutdown mode

BitField.name: IO_VDD_HSLV
BitField.description: High-speed IO at low VDD voltage configuration bit This bit can be set only with VDD below 2.5V

Enum.description: High-speed IO at low VDD voltage feature disabled (VDD can exceed 2.5 V)

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: High-speed IO at low VDD voltage feature enabled (VDD remains below 2.5 V)

BitField.name: IO_VDDIO2_HSLV
BitField.description: High-speed IO at low VDDIO2 voltage configuration bit This bit can be set only with VDDIO2 below 2.5 V.

Enum.name: B_0x1
Enum.description: High-speed IO at low VDDIO2 voltage feature enabled (VDDIO2 remains below 2.5 V)

BitField.name: TZEN
BitField.description: Global TrustZone security enable

BitField.name: NSBOOTADD0
BitField.description: Non-secure boot base address 0 The non-secure boot memory address can be programmed to any address in the valid address range with a granularity of 128 bytes. These bits correspond to address [31:7]. The NSBOOTADD0 option bytes are selected following the BOOT0 pin or nSWBOOT0 state. Examples: NSBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x0100000: Boot from non-secure Flash memory (0x0800 0000) NSBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x017F200: Boot from system memory bootloader (0x0BF9 0000) NSBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x0400000: Boot from non-secure SRAM1 on S-Bus (0x2000 0000)

BitField.name: NSBOOTADD1
BitField.description: Non-secure boot address 1 The non-secure boot memory address can be programmed to any address in the valid address range with a granularity of 128 bytes. These bits correspond to address [31:7]. The NSBOOTADD0 option bytes are selected following the BOOT0 pin or nSWBOOT0 state. Examples: NSBOOTADD1[24:0] = 0x0100000: Boot from non-secure Flash memory (0x0800 0000) NSBOOTADD1[24:0] = 0x017F200: Boot from system memory bootloader (0x0BF9 0000) NSBOOTADD1[24:0] = 0x0400000: Boot from non-secure SRAM1 on S-Bus (0x2000 0000)

BitField.name: BOOT_LOCK
BitField.description: Boot lock When set, the boot is always forced to base address value programmed in SECBOOTADD0[24:0] option bytes whatever the boot selection option. When set, this bit can only be cleared by an RDP at level 0.

BitField.name: SECBOOTADD0
BitField.description: Secure boot base address 0 The secure boot memory address can be programmed to any address in the valid address range with a granularity of 128 bytes. This bits correspond to address [31:7] The SECBOOTADD0 option bytes are selected following the BOOT0 pin or nSWBOOT0 state. Examples: SECBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x018 0000: Boot from secure Flash memory (0x0C00 0000) SECBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x01F F000: Boot from RSS (0x0FF8 0000) SECBOOTADD0[24:0] = 0x060 0000: Boot from secure SRAM1 on S-Bus (0x3000 0000)

BitField.name: MEMSET
BitField.description: Common memory x setup time These bits define the number of KCK_FMC (+1) clock cycles to set up the address before the command assertion (NWE, NOE), for NAND Flash read or write access to common memory space:

BitField.name: MEMWAIT
BitField.description: Common memory wait time These bits define the minimum number of KCK_FMC (+1) clock cycles to assert the command (NWE, NOE), for NAND Flash read or write access to common memory space. The duration of command assertion is extended if the wait signal (NWAIT) is active (low) at the end of the programmed value of KCK_FMC:

BitField.name: MEMHOLD
BitField.description: Common memory hold time These bits define the number of KCK_FMC clock cycles for write accesses and KCK_FMC+1 clock cycles for read accesses during which the address is held (and data for write accesses) after the command is de-asserted (NWE, NOE), for NAND Flash read or write access to common memory space:

BitField.name: MEMHIZ
BitField.description: Common memory x data bus Hi-Z time These bits define the number of KCK_FMC clock cycles during which the data bus is kept Hi-Z after the start of a NAND Flash write access to common memory space. This is only valid for write transactions:

Register.name: PATT
Register.description: The FMC_PATT read/write register contains the timing information for NAND Flash memory bank. It is used for 8-bit accesses to the attribute memory space of the NAND Flash for the last address write access if the timing must differ from that of previous accesses (for Ready/Busy management, refer to Section20.8.5: NAND Flash prewait feature).

BitField.name: ATTSET
BitField.description: Attribute memory setup time These bits define the number of KCK_FMC (+1) clock cycles to set up address before the command assertion (NWE, NOE), for NAND Flash read or write access to attribute memory space:

BitField.name: ATTWAIT
BitField.description: Attribute memory wait time These bits define the minimum number of x KCK_FMC (+1) clock cycles to assert the command (NWE, NOE), for NAND Flash read or write access to attribute memory space. The duration for command assertion is extended if the wait signal (NWAIT) is active (low) at the end of the programmed value of KCK_FMC:

BitField.name: ATTHOLD
BitField.description: Attribute memory hold time These bits define the number of KCK_FMC clock cycles during which the address is held (and data for write access) after the command de-assertion (NWE, NOE), for NAND Flash read or write access to attribute memory space:

BitField.name: ATTHIZ
BitField.description: Attribute memory data bus Hi-Z time These bits define the number of KCK_FMC clock cycles during which the data bus is kept in Hi-Z after the start of a NAND Flash write access to attribute memory space on socket. Only valid for writ transaction:

Register.name: ECCR
Register.description: This register contain the current error correction code value computed by the ECC computation modules of the FMC NAND controller. When the CPU reads/writes the data from a NAND Flash memory page at the correct address (refer to Section20.8.6: Computation of the error correction code (ECC) in NAND Flash memory), the data read/written from/to the NAND Flash memory are processed automatically by the ECC computation module. When X bytes have been read (according to the ECCPS field in the FMC_PCR registers), the CPU must read the computed ECC value from the FMC_ECC registers. It then verifies if these computed parity data are the same as the parity value recorded in the spare area, to determine whether a page is valid, and, to correct it otherwise. The FMC_ECCR register should be cleared after being read by setting the ECCEN bit to 0. To compute a new data block, the ECCEN bit must be set to 1.

BitField.name: ECC
BitField.description: ECC result This field contains the value computed by the ECC computation logic. Table167 describes the contents of these bit fields.

When the CPU reads/writes the data from a NAND Flash memory page at the correct address (refer to Section20.8.6: Computation of the error correction code (ECC) in NAND Flash memory), the data read/written from/to the NAND Flash memory are processed automatically by the ECC computation module. BitField.name: ECC
BitField.description: ECC result This field contains the value computed by the ECC computation logic. Table167 describes the contents of these bit fields.

BitField.name: B0OIE
BitField.description: Buffer 0 overflow interrupt enable This bit enables the buffer 0 overflow interrupt.

BitField.name: B1OIE
BitField.description: Buffer 1 overflow interrupt enable This bit enables the buffer 1 overflow interrupt.

BitField.name: B2OIE
BitField.description: Buffer 2 overflow interrupt enable This bit enables the buffer 2 overflow interrupt.

BitField.name: B3OIE
BitField.description: Buffer 3 overflow interrupt enable This bit enables the buffer 3 overflow interrupt.

BitField.name: AMEIE
BitField.description: AHB master error interrupt enable This bit enables the AHB master error interrupt.

BitField.name: BM192
BitField.description: 192 Block mode This bit defines the number of blocks per line

BitField.name: CE
BitField.description: Cache enable This bit enables the cache unit.

BitField.name: CL
BitField.description: Cache lock This bit lock the cache onto the buffer defined in the CLB field.

BitField.name: CLB
BitField.description: Cache lock buffer This field select the buffer on which the cache is locked.

BitField.name: FC
BitField.description: Force caching This bit force the caching into the cache regardless of the MPU attributes. The cache must be enable (CE bit set).

BitField.name: PD
BitField.description: Prefetch disable This bit disables the prefetch of the cache.

BitField.name: OC
BitField.description: Outter cachability This bit configure the cachability of an access generated by the GFXMMU cache.

BitField.name: OB
BitField.description: Outter bufferability This bit configure the bufferability of an access generated by the GFXMMU cache.

BitField.name: B0OF
BitField.description: Buffer 0 overflow flag This bit is set when an overflow occurs during the offset calculation of the buffer 0. It is cleared by writing 1 to CB0OF.

BitField.name: B1OF
BitField.description: Buffer 1 overflow flag This bit is set when an overflow occurs during the offset calculation of the buffer 1. It is cleared by writing 1 to CB1OF.

BitField.name: B2OF
BitField.description: Buffer 2 overflow flag This bit is set when an overflow occurs during the offset calculation of the buffer 2. It is cleared by writing 1 to CB2OF.

BitField.name: B3OF
BitField.description: Buffer 3 overflow flag This bit is set when an overflow occurs during the offset calculation of the buffer 3. It is cleared by writing 1 to CB3OF.

BitField.name: AMEF
BitField.description: AHB master error flag This bit is set when an AHB error happens during a transaction. It is cleared by writing 1 to CAMEF.

BitField.name: CB0OF
BitField.description: Clear buffer 0 overflow flag Writing 1 clears the buffer 0 overflow flag in the GFXMMU_SR register.

BitField.name: CB1OF
BitField.description: Clear buffer 1 overflow flag Writing 1 clears the buffer 1 overflow flag in the GFXMMU_SR register.

BitField.name: CB2OF
BitField.description: Clear buffer 2 overflow flag Writing 1 clears the buffer 2 overflow flag in the GFXMMU_SR register.

BitField.name: CB3OF
BitField.description: Clear buffer 3 overflow flag Writing 1 clears the buffer 3 overflow flag in the GFXMMU_SR register.

BitField.name: CAMEF
BitField.description: Clear AHB master error flag Writing 1 clears the AHB master error flag in the GFXMMU_SR register.

BitField.name: FF
BitField.description: Force flush When set, the cache entries are flushed. This bit is reset by hardware when the flushing is complete. Write 0 has no effect.

BitField.name: FI
BitField.description: Force invalidate When set, the cache entries are invalidated. This bit is reset by hardware when the invalidation is complete. Write 0 has no effect.

BitField.name: DV
BitField.description: Default value This field indicates the default 32-bit value which is returned when a master accesses a virtual memory location not physically mapped.

BitField.name: PBO
BitField.description: Physical buffer offset Offset of the physical buffer.

BitField.name: PBBA
BitField.description: Physical buffer base address Base address MSB of the physical buffer.

BitField.name: PBO
BitField.description: Physical buffer offset Offset of the physical buffer.

BitField.name: PBBA
BitField.description: Physical buffer base address Base address MSB of the physical buffer.
